statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-102870 (GHSA-g27p-qf6j-c96c) is an ASP.NET Core remote code execution issue in the Blazor WebAssembly debug proxy: values from the application being debugged are embedded without consistent escaping in C# source that the proxy compiles to evaluate debugger expressions, so attacker-controlled data can run code on a developer's machine. Microsoft lists Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server and Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.DevServer before 10.0.14 as affected and 10.0.14 as fixed, and says that updating the shared runtime is not a substitute for updating these packages (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-g27p-qf6j-c96c, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/445, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/492). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries; 10.0.15-r0 is built from the v10.0.115 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v10.0.115). Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside their nupkg and tar.gz archives: none of them contains the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server or Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.DevServer package or assembly, or the BrowserDebugHost debug proxy; these packages are restored from NuGet into application projects and are not part of the ASP.NET Core shared framework.

CVE-2026-102870 (GHSA-g27p-qf6j-c96c) is an ASP.NET Core remote code execution issue in the Blazor WebAssembly debug proxy: values from the application being debugged are embedded without consistent escaping in C# source that the proxy compiles to evaluate debugger expressions, so attacker-controlled data can run code on a developer's machine. Microsoft lists Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server and Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.DevServer before 10.0.14 as affected and 10.0.14 as fixed, and says that updating the shared runtime is not a substitute for updating these packages (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-g27p-qf6j-c96c, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/445, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/492). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.24 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries; 10.0.15-r0 is built from the v10.0.115 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v10.0.115). Scanned all 154 packages of the seven published builds (10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.12-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside their nupkg and tar.gz archives: none of them contains the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server or Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.DevServer package or assembly, or the BrowserDebugHost debug proxy; these packages are restored from NuGet into application projects and are not part of the ASP.NET Core shared framework.
